plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, SPAL) to zero.
Exit SMCI due to the scanner's SELL flag.
Trim SMH and QQQI to reduce concentration and comply with mandate limits.
This approach aims for a stable book with minimal drawdown.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions. Expect lower volatility and smaller drawdowns.

plan: For balanced growth, trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU) to small positions.
Sell SPAL and SMCI due to scanner flags and to reduce overall leverage.
Trim QQQI to meet concentration limits.
Add COP, a top-quality scanner long setup, to diversify and add growth potential.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality long setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: For aggressive growth, add to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU) to increase exposure.
Sell SPAL and SMCI due to scanner flags.
Trim QQQI to meet concentration limits.
Buy COP, a strong scanner long setup, with a larger allocation to lean into growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of higher potential drawdowns and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: For income, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, SPAL) to zero.
Exit SMCI due to the scanner's SELL flag.
Trim SMH to reduce high-beta exposure.
Add to QQQI to increase income-generating positions for steady distributions.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, prioritizing yield and capital preservation. It significantly reduces high-beta and leveraged exposure, focusing on income-generating ETFs. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fall in market downturns.
